method: Evidence/rights gates first. Placement blends interest, relevance, novelty, familiarity, consequence, source confidence, originality, visual strength, freshness, radar context and rotation pressure, then applies a diversity rerank so nearby homepage slots prefer different categories and subjects. Editorial story-overrides are applied before ranking so approved headlines and imagery persist across generated homepage surfaces.

feature.headline: Up to 90% of a building can now be made inside this Burlington factory.
feature.deck: SEKISUI's $15-million Canadian hub is targeting schools, housing and care buildings.
feature.label: Made in Burlington
feature.alt: Diagram showing building modules made in a factory and assembled into a mid-rise building.
feature.storyGoal: Turn a new investment announcement into an understandable Made in Burlington story about what the factory makes, how much work can happen indoors and the scale SEKISUI says it is targeting.

feature.headline: Oakville approved a 1,000-space Costco near Burloak. The plan has four access points.
feature.deck: The site plan shows a gas bar, surface and underground parking, and four proposed access points.
feature.label: Development
feature.alt: Costco storefront and entrance in a suburban shopping area.
feature.storyGoal: Explain the recently approved Costco site plan near Burloak through the practical questions Burlington drivers care about: status, parking, access and what is still unconfirmed.

feature.headline: How bad is crime in Burlington, really?
feature.deck: One category of crime is moving the wrong way.
feature.label: Public safety
feature.alt: Halton Regional Police vehicle behind crime-scene tape.
feature.storyGoal: Help Burlington readers understand what the best comparable crime data actually says, and where a regional score cannot answer a city-level question.

feature.headline: A Burlington gathering place closed. The problem wasn’t demand.
feature.deck: A large community and a last fundraising push could not solve an occupancy and renovation problem.
feature.label: Local business
feature.alt: The interior of Nostalgia Candy Café, with a blue counter, wooden tables and a wall logo.
feature.storyGoal: Explain why a well-liked local cafe closed without treating a fundraiser page as the whole story.

rail.headline: Burlington has spent more than $90 million on stormwater since 2015. What changed?
rail.deck: Tuck Creek shows what the money has changed, and why some major flood work is still unfinished.
rail.label: Infrastructure
rail.alt: Timeline showing Burlington flood protection work from the 2014 storm through 2028.
rail.storyGoal: Explain what Burlington's more than $90 million in stormwater investment has physically changed, using Tuck Creek as a concrete example while being explicit about unfinished and paused work.

rail.headline: Two Burlington roads will stay fully closed into September.
rail.deck: Spruce Avenue is closed through Sept. 4. Britannia Road has no through traffic through the end of September.
rail.label: Roads
rail.alt: Road construction and lane restrictions on a Burlington arterial road.
rail.storyGoal: Give Burlington residents a concise, verified list of significant full municipal road closures that continue into September, while separating them from ordinary lane restrictions.

rail.headline: E-scooter injuries are rising. Burlington’s rules are stricter than you might think.
rail.deck: Most public roads and sidewalks in Burlington are still off-limits.
rail.label: Transportation
rail.alt: A person riding an e-scooter along the right side of a suburban street.
rail.storyGoal: Connect the national rise in e-scooter injuries to Burlington’s narrow Centennial Trail-only rules.
